profile.headline: Building the Future of Grant Productivity | Automating Grant Research + Submission-Ready Packages for Mission Driven Projects | MBA SaaS Founder
profile.summary:
Most mission-driven teams are buried in grant chaos, scattered spreadsheets, and under-resourced tech.

I’m Njeri Cooper, a full-stack software engineer and SaaS founder building systems that help nonprofits and community orgs do more of the work that matters.

By day, I’m a Web Developer and Software Engineer with 8+ years of experience shipping and maintaining production web systems. At Youth Villages I:

- Build donor-facing event and campaign microsites that support large-scale fundraising

- Maintain and secure multi-environment infrastructure (DigitalOcean, Linux, Apache, Nginx, implement security best practices)

- Recently secured $2,500 in DigitalOcean nonprofit credits, effectively reducing hosting costs by 100% across 7 production sites

By night and weekends, I’m founder of Subvent, a software that’s helping grant and donor-funded teams move from grant overwhelm to clarity by bringing discovery, application, and reporting into one guided workflow.

I also share the journey and the playbook through:

- MBA SaaS Founder (newsletter): lessons from building Subvent as a technical founder and MBA student, focused on validation, customer conversations, and traction experiments

- The MBA Founder Podcast (co-host): candid conversations with student founders about building SaaS, getting customers, and staying sane in the process

Thread through everything: I design and build funding systems, from the infrastructure behind donation flows and event registrations to the software and stories that help mission-driven teams raise more and operate with less chaos.

If you have a mission-driven org or are community leader trying to slay grants on your own feel free to connect or DM me “SUBVENT” to follow the build and get early beta access details.

If you’re a SaaS founder, DM me “CHAT” to have a convo on The MBA Founder podcast.

positions.title: Web Developer and Software Engineer
positions.description:
As part of the Youth Villages Digital Marketing Communications (marcom) department, the duties of my role include but are not limited to:
Maintaining development, testing, and production environments’ server and hosting. Developing custom code for donor-facing event and donation based campaign micro-sites. Maintaining all brand development, environments, and server infrastructure. Developing and analyzing value-based monthly KPI metrics using Google analytics (GA4 and universal analytics).

- Using clean, sustainable and modular frontend code based in HTML, CSS and JavaScript to improve donor / user experience.
 
- Focusing on non-profit and e-commerce best practices to drive donors to the most important call to action. 

- Maintaining website environments using Digital Ocean Apache 2 and Nginx IP-address based servers. Implementing security headers, managing TLS and TCP versions, SSL certificates with lets encrypt in command line terminal to ensure site reliability.

- Designing and developing event registration websites and attendee facing mobile applications using CVENT and event management platform. 

- Building internal and external facing interest forms using CRM 123FormBuilder. Ensuring form response emails deliverability have no CORS issues. Assisted with input field labeling that incorporates mapping into SalesForce.

- HTML-based email design, development, and testing in SalesForce Marketing Cloud.

- Optimized server environment sizes and switched to next-generation media files to reduce hosting costs by 25% annually.

Skills Used:
- Graphic Design
- Communication and collaboration with key stakeholders, project managers and team leads
- Asking for and accepting constructive criticism 
- Site reliability engineering, web accessibility and web best practices
- Event management, registration page and process building, event mobile application development with CVENT

projects.title: Subvent Advisory Board
projects.description:
Subvent’s Board Project is a lightweight, high-accountability advisory and peer board that accelerate traction and strengthen execution. This board meets on a consistent cadence and supports real-time decision-making as we scale an AI-assisted grant management platform for mission-driven organizations.

What we’re doing with the board

- Running a 90-minute board meeting every 4 weeks, replacing that week’s class/cohort session
- Using a structured format: 10 minutes per founder (5-minute update + 5-minute Q&A) to keep feedback focused and actionable
- Working with 2-3 non-executive board members (plus a chair) to bring outside perspective, challenge assumptions, and share networks
- Maintaining ongoing informal communication between meetings so board members arrive with context and can help remove blockers quickly

How we operate

- Sharing a 1-page board report at least 48 hours in advance (headline, biggest learning, obstacles, priorities, and North Star metrics)
- Centering the conversation on execution: customer acquisition, growth levers, experimentation, and measurable progress
- Using the board to pressure-test strategy, pricing, positioning, and go-to-market then turning insights into weekly priorities

Why it matters

This project is designed to create consistent accountability, better decisions, and faster learning cycles so Subvent can keep building what customers will pay for, improve traction, and stay focused on the metrics that matter.
